questions.question: Pre-eclampsia is diagnosed at what BP threshold after 20 weeks' gestation?
questions.explanation: BP ≥140/90 mmHg on two occasions ≥4 hours apart after 20 weeks + proteinuria or end-organ dysfunction = pre-eclampsia.

explanations.A: This is the Stage 1 hypertension cutoff, not the pre-eclampsia threshold.
explanations.B: BP ≥140/90 mmHg on two occasions ≥4 hours apart after 20 weeks + proteinuria or end-organ dysfunction = pre-eclampsia.
explanations.D: ≥160/110 defines pre-eclampsia with severe features, not the diagnosis itself.

questions.subject: OBG

questions.question: First step in Neonatal Resuscitation Program after birth:
questions.explanation: Initial steps per NRP: warm, dry, position airway, clear secretions, stimulate.

explanations.A: Cord clamping follows the initial steps.
explanations.B: Initial steps per NRP: warm, dry, position airway, clear secretions, stimulate.
explanations.C: Oxygen only if HR <100 and PPV has failed.
explanations.D: Chest compressions only if HR <60 after effective PPV.

questions.explanation: Term newborn needs ET tube 3.0–3.5 mm uncuffed.

explanations.B: Term newborn needs ET tube 3.0–3.5 mm uncuffed.

questions.subject: Pediatric

questions.question: MgSO4 therapeutic serum level in eclampsia is:
questions.explanation: Therapeutic serum magnesium level = 4–7 mEq/L for eclampsia prophylaxis.

explanations.B: Therapeutic serum magnesium level = 4–7 mEq/L for eclampsia prophylaxis.
explanations.C: 8–10 mEq/L → loss of deep tendon reflexes (toxic).
explanations.D: >10 mEq/L → respiratory depression; stop infusion and give calcium gluconate.
